nodes.label: VN
nodes.capability: No need for description due to input/output circuit

nodes.label: GC(granule)
nodes.comments:
Hypothesis (role; functional-need): The FRG needs a context expansion stage before the Purkinje cells; the reviewed literature on the flocculus [Ito, 1982] does not state this role for its granule cells.
Granule cells relaying mossy fibre input as parallel fibres
nodes.requirement: Expand the head velocity context from [U.VN] under gain control by [U.GoC(golgi)] and send it to [U.PC(purkinje)].
nodes.requirementRealization: [U.VN] supplies head velocity, [U.GoC(golgi)] scales it, and the expanded code goes to [U.PC(purkinje)].
nodes.capability: Expansion recoding of mossy fibre input [Ito, 1982].
nodes.mechanism: Many granule cells each sample a few mossy fibres.

items.rationale: The FRG needs a context expansion stage before the Purkinje cells; the reviewed literature on the flocculus [Ito, 1982] does not state this role for its granule cells.

nodes.label: PC(purkinje)
nodes.comments: Purkinje cells learning the VOR gain
nodes.requirement: Combine the context from [U.GC(granule)] with the error from [U.IO] and inhibit [U.FTN].
nodes.requirementRealization: [U.GC(granule)] gives the context, [U.IO] the error, and the corrected gain goes to [U.FTN].
nodes.capability: Supervised learning of the VOR gain [Ito, 1982].
nodes.mechanism: Climbing fibre input depresses co-active parallel fibre synapses.

nodes.label: IO
nodes.comments:
Hypothesis (transmitter; homology): Olivary neurons are glutamatergic in the monkey [Lisberger, 1994]; no paper found reports the transmitter of the olivary neurons that project to the human flocculus.
Retinal slip error signal
nodes.requirement: Signal the retinal slip error from [U.VN] to [U.PC(purkinje)].
nodes.requirementRealization: The input from [U.VN] is turned into an error sent to [U.PC(purkinje)].
nodes.mechanism: Complex spikes report the retinal slip.

items.rationale: Olivary neurons are glutamatergic in the monkey [Lisberger, 1994]; no paper found reports the transmitter of the olivary neurons that project to the human flocculus.

nodes.label: GoC(golgi)
nodes.comments:
Hypothesis (population; analogy): Golgi cells form a distinct inhibitory population of the cerebellar cortex in the cat [Eccles, 1967]; no paper found defines this population in the flocculus.
Golgi cells controlling the granule cell gain
nodes.requirement: Scale the granule cell gain from the input of [U.VN] and send it to [U.GC(granule)].
nodes.requirementRealization: The input from [U.VN] sets the inhibition sent to [U.GC(granule)].
nodes.mechanism: Golgi cell inhibition limits granule cell firing.

items.rationale: Golgi cells form a distinct inhibitory population of the cerebellar cortex in the cat [Eccles, 1967]; no paper found defines this population in the flocculus.

nodes.label: FTN
nodes.comments: Floccular target neurons in the vestibular nuclei; noROI(output)
nodes.capability: No need for description due to input/output circuit

edges.pointersOnLiterature: Mossy fibres from the vestibular nuclei terminate on granule cells of the flocculus in the rabbit.

edges.comments:
Hypothesis (direction; indirect): Vestibular and olivary activity are correlated in the monkey [Lisberger, 1994]; no paper found states that the vestibular nuclei drive the inferior olive rather than the reverse.
co-activation of vestibular and olivary neurons
edges.pointersOnLiterature: Activity in the vestibular nuclei and the inferior olive was correlated during adaptation of the reflex in monkeys.

items.rationale: Vestibular and olivary activity are correlated in the monkey [Lisberger, 1994]; no paper found states that the vestibular nuclei drive the inferior olive rather than the reverse.

edges.pointersOnLiterature: Mossy fibre collaterals from the vestibular nuclei also contact Golgi cells in the granular layer of the flocculus.
Parallel fibres of the granule cells make excitatory synapses on the dendrites of Purkinje cells in the flocculus.
Climbing fibres from the inferior olive terminate on floccular Purkinje cells and carry the retinal slip signal.

edges.comments:
Hypothesis (existence; homology): Golgi cells inhibit granule cells in the cat cerebellar cortex [Eccles, 1967]; no paper found states this projection in the flocculus of the modelled species.
inhibition
edges.pointersOnLiterature: Golgi cells exert a powerful inhibitory action on the granule cells of the cerebellar cortex in the cat.

items.rationale: Golgi cells inhibit granule cells in the cat cerebellar cortex [Eccles, 1967]; no paper found states this projection in the flocculus of the modelled species.

edges.pointersOnLiterature: Floccular Purkinje cells inhibit a subset of neurons in the vestibular nuclei called floccular target neurons.

collections.comments: The floccular cortex is split into granule, Purkinje and Golgi cells, which differ in transmitter and projection target [Ito, 1982].

nodes.label: R.VOR-Adaptation
nodes.comments: TLF: adapt the gain of the vestibulo-ocular reflex; Depends on hypotheses: H1, H2, H3, H5
nodes.requirement: Adapt the reflex gain from the input of [U.VN] and drive [U.FTN] through [R.Context], [R.Learning] and [R.Gain-Control].
nodes.requirementRealization: [U.VN] enters through [U.GC(granule)], [U.GoC(golgi)] and [U.IO]; [U.PC(purkinje)] sends the corrected gain to [U.FTN].
nodes.mechanism: Error-driven plasticity in the floccular cortex.

nodes.label: R.Context
nodes.comments: Context representation read out by Purkinje cells; Depends on hypotheses: H1
nodes.requirement: Represent the head velocity context with [U.GC(granule)] and read it out with [U.PC(purkinje)].
nodes.requirementRealization: [U.VN] and [U.GoC(golgi)] drive [U.GC(granule)]; [U.PC(purkinje)] combines it with [U.IO] and inhibits [U.FTN].
nodes.mechanism: Parallel fibres converge on Purkinje cells.

nodes.label: R.Learning
nodes.comments: Error-driven learning of the gain; Depends on hypotheses: H2
nodes.requirement: Correct the gain stored by [U.PC(purkinje)] with the error from [U.IO].
nodes.requirementRealization: [U.VN] drives [U.IO]; [U.PC(purkinje)] combines the error with [U.GC(granule)] and inhibits [U.FTN].

nodes.label: R.Gain-Control
nodes.comments: Feedforward control of the granule cell gain; Depends on hypotheses: H1, H3, H5
nodes.requirement: Keep the activity of [U.GC(granule)] in range using [U.GoC(golgi)].
nodes.requirementRealization: [U.VN] drives both [U.GoC(golgi)] and [U.GC(granule)]; the scaled code goes to [U.PC(purkinje)].
nodes.mechanism: Golgi cell inhibition divides granule cell activity.
